ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, $E$ and $F$ are the midpoints of the sides $CD$ and $AD$ respectively, $CF$ intersects $EA$ and $EB$ at points $M$ and $N$ respectively. Given $AB=8$ and $BC=12$, what is the length of $MN$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, extend BE and AD to meet at point Q. Since quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle, $BC=12$, thus $\angle BAD=90^\circ$, $AD=BC=12$, $AD\parallel BC$. Since F is the midpoint of AD, it follows that $AF=DF=6$. In $\triangle DCF$, by the Pythagorean theorem, we get: $CF=\sqrt{DF^2+DC^2}=\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10$. Since $AD\parallel BC$, it follows that $\angle Q=\angle EBC$. Since E is the midpoint of CD and $CD=8$, it follows that $CE=DE=4$. In $\triangle DQE$ and $\triangle CBE$, we have $\begin{cases}
\angle DEQ=\angle BEC\\ 
\angle Q=\angle EBC\\ 
DE=CE
\end{cases}$, thus $\triangle DQE\cong \triangle CBE$ (AAS), hence $DQ=BC=12$, that is $QF=12+6=18$. Since $AD\parallel BC$, it follows that $\triangle QNF\sim \triangle BNC$, hence $\frac{FN}{CN}=\frac{QF}{BC}=\frac{18}{12}=\frac{3}{2}$. Since $CF=10$, we get $CN=4$, $FN=6$. As illustrated, extend CF and BA to meet at W. Since $WB\parallel CD$, it follows that $\angle W=\angle DCF$. In $\triangle WAF$ and $\triangle CDF$, we have $\begin{cases}
\angle W=\angle DCF\\ 
AF=DF\\ 
\angle AFW=\angle CFD
\end{cases}$, thus $\triangle WAF\cong \triangle CDF$ (AAS), hence $CD=AW=8$, $BW=16$, $CF=FW=10$. Because $AB\parallel CD$, it follows that $\triangle CME\sim \triangle WMA$, hence $\frac{CM}{MW}=\frac{CE}{AW}$, solving this we get: $CM=\frac{20}{3}$, hence $MN=CM-CN=\frac{20}{3}-4=\boxed{\frac{8}{3}}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, $E$ and $F$ are the midpoints of the sides $CD$ and $AD$ respectively, $CF$ intersects $EA$ and $EB$ at points $M$ and $N$ respectively. Given $AB=8$ and $BC=12$, what is the length of $MN$?
raw_record.answer: As shown in the figure, extend $BE$ and $AD$ to meet at point $Q$. Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rectangle, $BC=12$, thus $\angle BAD=90^\circ$, $AD=BC=12$, $AD\parallel BC$. Since $F$ is the midpoint of $AD$, it follows that $AF=DF=6$. In $\triangle DCF$, by the Pythagorean theorem, we get $CF=\sqrt{DF^2+DC^2}=\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10$. Since $AD\parallel BC$, it follows that $\angle Q=\angle EBC$. Since $E$ is the midpoint of $CD$ and $CD=8$, it follows that $CE=DE=4$. In $\triangle DQE$ and $\triangle CBE$, we have $\angle DEQ=\angle BEC$, $\angle Q=\angle EBC$, and $DE=CE$, thus $\triangle DQE\cong\triangle CBE$ (AAS), hence $DQ=BC=12$, that is $QF=12+6=18$. Since $AD\parallel BC$, it follows that $\triangle QNF\sim\triangle BNC$, hence $\frac{FN}{CN}=\frac{QF}{BC}=\frac{18}{12}=\frac{3}{2}$. Since $CF=10$, we get $CN=4$, $FN=6$. Extend $CF$ and $BA$ to meet at $W$. Since $WB\parallel CD$, it follows that $\angle W=\angle DCF$. In $\triangle WAF$ and $\triangle CDF$, we have $\angle W=\angle DCF$, $AF=DF$, and $\angle AFW=\angle CFD$, thus $\triangle WAF\cong\triangle CDF$ (AAS), hence $CD=AW=8$, $BW=16$, $CF=FW=10$. Because $AB\parallel CD$, it follows that $\triangle CME\sim\triangle WMA$, hence $\frac{CM}{MW}=\frac{CE}{AW}$, solving this we get $CM=\frac{20}{3}$, hence $MN=CM-CN=\frac{20}{3}-4=\boxed{\frac{8}{3}}$.
raw_record.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a rectangle ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right. E is located at the midpoint of the right side CD, and F is located at the midpoint of the upper side AD. Segment CF connects from the lower-right point C to the midpoint F of the upper side, and intersects AE and BE at M and N respectively, where M is above N. Then reason: By the coordinate method, let B=(0,0), A=(0,8), C=(12,0), D=(12,8), which satisfies AB=8, BC=12. Because E is the midpoint of CD, E=(12,4); because F is the midpoint of AD, F=(6,8). Parametrize CF: P(t)=C+t(F-C)=(12-6t,8t), where t=0 is C and t=1 is F. Line AE can be written as (12s,8-4s). Solving 12-6t=12s, 8t=8-4s gives t_M=2/3. Line BE can be written as (12r,4r). Solving 12-6t=12r, 8t=4r gives t_N=2/5. The length of CF is sqrt((12-6)^2+(0-8)^2)=sqrt(36+64)=10. Therefore MN=(t_M-t_N)·CF=(2/3-2/5)·10=(4/15)·10=8/3.
